newsitem.title: UK: Gilts end higher after big public debt repayment.
newsitem.headline: Gilts end higher after big public debt repayment.

text.p: 1520 GMT - Gilts end Monday with healthy gains after boost from above-forecast debt repayment, helped by solid start from U.S. Treasuries and Dow Jones. * September gilt future settled 14/32 higher at 115-02

"The bigger-than-expected surplus seems to have been driven primarily by a large increase in VAT receipts. That is a reflection of the strength of the domestic economy," said Rob Hayward, economist at BankAmerica.
Just as importantly for the market, the Dow Jones index of leading U.S. shares did not plunge as many expected in New York and U.S. T-bonds managed to hold a firm tone.
The September T-bond was 15/32 higher at 114-03 by 1530 GMT.
Tuesday's calendar offers little of substance but on Wednesday, key retail sales figures will be released.

The Reuter consensus forecast suggests retail sales rose by 0.3 percent in July compared with June's 0.6 percent, although this would push the year-on-year rate of growth up to 5.8 percent from 5.4 in June.
"Without doubt Wednesday's retail sales figure stands head and shoulders above the other economic numbers this week," said Don Smith, strategist at HSBC Markets.
"Concerns about rampant consumer spending are crucial in influencing the market's perceptions about interest rate prospects."
Smith said the market would view the risks on the upside but if the data shows the pace of sales growth easing, the long end would be the chief beneficiary.

"(If the figures are soft), longs would outperform, especially if investors begin to ponder on the possibility that the economy, inflation and interest rates could weaken significantly next year," he said.
The gilt/Bund spread edged in to 149 basis points from 151 late on Friday, while the December short sterling future shed just one basis point to 92.63.
It is discounting one further quarter-point interest rate rise by the year-end. -- Mike Peacock, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7708
